_readme: Canonical cross-platform contract for the sponsor-type pattern lists (issue #147)
and the funder-classification confidence ladder (issue #152).
This file is the single source of truth. Python and Swift (BioMedLit) each carry
their own transcription of these values, and each platform's test suite asserts
its behaviour equals this file exactly. Editing one platform without editing this
file fails that platform's parity test; editing this file without updating the
other fails theirs. That is the point: silent divergence becomes impossible.
Android carries no funder or sponsor classifier, so it is not a party to this
contract — unlike data_availability_patterns.json, which binds all three.
PATTERNS. The split into two halves is significant and is NOT presentational:
- determine_sponsor_type() / FundingAnalyzer.determineSponsorType tests the
government half first, so one public agency outranks any number of
universities alongside it.
- classify_funder_name() / FundingAnalyzer.classifyFunder walks government
then academic, which covers exactly their concatenation in order. Adding or
removing a pattern changes the industry boundary, which is measured against
funder_names.json; moving one between halves changes the sponsor tier and
the reported confidence, but not the boundary.
CONFIDENCES. The value each classification layer reports, asserted
behaviourally: a test classifies a representative funder and compares the
confidence, rather than reading the constant. Swift's constants are private, and
behaviour is what actually reaches a user in any case. Python reported a flat
0.8 for both non-industry halves until #152, where Swift had always reported
0.85 and 0.80 -- a divergence the boolean-scored funder corpus could not see.
The ladder must stay strictly descending: a known registry DOI outranks a named
public body, which outranks a generic institutional word, which outranks a
generic company form, which outranks no match at all.
PATTERN PROBES. One representative funder name per pattern. A string-for-string
pin catches the platforms drifting apart; it cannot catch a pattern that never
matched anything on any of them, because all copies agree on the same typo.
Every pattern above must match at least one probe name here, and every probe
name must classify as non-industry. Mirrors the same invariant in
data_availability_patterns.json.
Do not regenerate this file mechanically from any one platform. Change it by hand,
deliberately, as part of a change that touches both.
See doc/cross_platform/transparency_parity/README.md.
